problem: The left and right halves of the round output are stated the wrong way round. The chapter's own formula gives L₁ = R₀ and R₁ = L₀⊕F(R₀,K₁), so the RIGHT half of the output is L₀⊕F(R₀,K₁) and the LEFT half is R₀. The text says the opposite, and this contradicts the formula, the figure and Worked example 1 (where L₁ = 0110 = R₀ and R₁ = 1001 = L₀⊕F).
fix: After one round the halves have changed places. The left half of the output equals R₀, and the right half of the output is L₀⊕F(R₀,K₁).

problem: Feeding Lᵢ as the right input and Rᵢ as the left input into the round formula returns the two halves in swapped positions: the round outputs Rᵢ₋₁ on the left and Lᵢ₋₁ on the right, i.e. Rᵢ₋₁ Lᵢ₋₁, not Lᵢ₋₁ Rᵢ₋₁. As written a student may think the ordering comes back exactly as the plaintext.
fix: Say: use the same subkey Kᵢ and you recover the two halves Lᵢ₋₁ and Rᵢ₋₁, with Rᵢ₋₁ appearing on the left and Lᵢ₋₁ on the right (one extra swap, which is why the last-round swap convention matters).
